question: Does the unchanged P0565 coherent-core/twisted-outskirts rule predict the sign of a physical baryon-tensor response in both A383 and MS2137?
interpretation: prospective two-cluster data-channel transfer; neither target supplied a morphology label or tensor response to P0564 or P0565

field_hypothesis.environment_input: Q is constructed from projected ACCEPT gas mass modulated only in angle by Chandra morphology, plus F160W light normalized to the Tian stellar-mass anchor

coordinates_and_split.catalog_x_conversion: internal x_arcsec=-delta_x_west_arcsec so positive x is east; y_arcsec=delta_y_north_arcsec
coordinates_and_split.within_family_rule: hold out the lexicographically last image in every family with at least three images; two-image families remain training-only
coordinates_and_split.source_positions: profile independently on the training images in every exact fit

registered_map_construction.hst_negative_flux_rule: subtract frozen outer-annulus median and clip negative flux to zero
registered_map_construction.xray_observation_combination: sum each observation sky histogram divided by its header exposure

frozen_sign_gate.rule: t=-0.3 only if inner correlation exceeds its threshold AND outer cos2 alignment is below its threshold; otherwise t=+0.3
frozen_sign_gate.grid_clipping_disclosure: The inherited P0564/P0565 120-arcsec descriptor was evaluated on a square map extending only +/-60 arcsec; it is therefore a full-square outer descriptor rather than a complete circular 120-arcsec aperture. P0566 reproduces that limitation exactly so the transfer is unchanged.

physical_tensor_map.accept_projection: exact line-of-sight projection of contiguous piecewise-constant ACCEPT ne shells with mu_e=1.17
physical_tensor_map.gas_angular_modulation: 3-arcsec Gaussian-smoothed, point-source-masked Chandra rate; divide by one-pixel annular mean; square-root power; cap to [0.25,4]; renormalize each annulus to mean one
physical_tensor_map.stellar_amplitude: normalize the positive F160W map to the Tian BCG stellar-mass anchor

response_and_exact_score.exploratory_grid_rule: retain only couplings with minimum tensor permittivity eigenvalue above 0.05; the optimum cannot modify the frozen gate
response_and_exact_score.source_plane_rule: unweighted training-family source mean with held-out source-plane separation, as in P0563

comparators.baryons_GR: s=-2 makes the extra RAR force invisible to light; six geometry nuisances, zero halo parameters
comparators.RAR_equal_light_matter: s=0 applies the fixed RAR enhancement equally to light and matter; six geometry nuisances
comparators.compact_halo: baryonic GR plus an object-specific non-singular isothermal ellipsoid and shear; eight fitted per-cluster lens/geometry parameters, used only as a dark-matter-style yardstick

claim_limits: The two targets were selected after P0565, although their new morphology descriptors and tensor responses were unread when this protocol was frozen.
The sign gate still contains two thresholds derived post hoc from one negative and three positive systems; two transfers cannot establish a population law.
The outer descriptor inherits a clipped-aperture implementation and must be retested later on genuinely larger common maps.
F160W light has no resolved mass-to-light map, and X-ray brightness modulates angular gas shape but does not set gas mass.
The source-plane response is a conditioning-resistant directional diagnostic; only exact image-plane roots are the primary score.
The compact-halo comparator is flexible and fitted separately per cluster, so it is a performance yardstick rather than a parameter-matched model.
This is a projected weak-field equation, not a covariant four-dimensional theory.
No formula can be promoted from P0566.
